title: One layer stack: Modal, bell and account own Escape, outside-press, keys

body:
## Summary
The shell's three overlays (Modal, the bell tray, the account panel) each own a private copy of dismissal: their own document keydown, their own outside-press, their own focus return and, for Modal, their own scroll lock. Nothing in the app can say what is on top. The app's key guards therefore sniff the DOM for `aria-modal` (lib/board/keys.ts:55), and that sniff cannot see the shell's own trays. This card adds one owned layer stack (`components/ui/layers.ts`) that these three surfaces push into and `overlayOpen` reads from, so 'what is open, and who gets this key' becomes a query.

## Description
`layers.ts` holds a module-level ordered stack of `{id, kind: 'modal'|'tray'|'popover', contains(node), anchor?}` and pure queries over it: `escapeTarget`, `outsidePress`, `trapOwner`, `lockTransition` (reference-counted) and `claimsKeys`. A `useLayer(open, {kind, panelRef, anchorRef, onDismiss})` hook pushes on open and removes by id on close (identity, never position). One document keydown and one pointerdown listener route each event to the top entry only. Modal keeps its focus-restore and trap logic but runs it only as `trapOwner`. Its lock goes through the refcount. NotificationBell and UserMenu delete their listener effects and keep their focus hand-offs. `overlayOpen(root, layers = openLayers())` returns true for any open layer, with the loupe exception unchanged, so the Board, the calendar week, the pipeline canvas and the gesture layer all stop deciding items behind a tray. The `cancelBubble` yield (c6ac2db) stays as the compatibility rule for popovers that are not on the stack yet (Hint, Select, the three ContextMenus). They are the next adopters, left out of this write set to keep it to one builder.

The cheap fix, `data-keys-block` on the two trays, closes acceptance case 1 only. It leaves the double-acting Escape (case 2), the nested-modal Escape and lock (cases 3 and 4), and the next tray someone adds, which will be invisible again. The stack is the move that stops the shell being the reason every key guard needs a DOM sniff.

## Flow
- bell opens -> useLayer pushes {id:'bell', kind:'tray'}
- user presses A on /board -> useBoardKeys -> overlayOpen() sees the tray -> null; nothing is decided
- user presses Escape -> the stack's single listener -> escapeTarget = 'bell' -> bell closes, focus returns to the trigger; Board's close does not run because boardKeyAction yields while a non-loupe layer is open
- a Modal opened over a Modal -> Escape pops the inner one; the lock holds until the last modal leaves

## Expected impact
A real misdecision class closes: a batch approve, reject or clear through an open tray, and an Escape that wipes a multi-pick. The shell's three overlays shrink by their duplicated listener effects (~60 lines). Every future overlay gets dismissal, lock and key-claim by calling one hook, and the four key guards stop depending on an attribute convention.

## Evaluation
Claim: the shell's overlays become one owned stack, and the app's key guards consult it.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-6 and 8 fail: no layers module, no layer argument; case 7 is a guard)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - new tests/golden-path/layer-stack.probe.spec.ts (pure stack queries plus a source ratchet) and extended board.probe.spec.ts overlayOpen cases, Node probe lane, no DOM
Result: better
Gate: architecture

body:
## Summary
The bell's storage card is the app's most expensive news: a full quota means the hour of work on screen is not being saved. Today it is a dead end. It shows a paragraph, a `phase · message` line and a 'dismiss' that erases the fact. This card makes it a remedy. Each failure kind gets the one verb that fixes it, every step that failed to save is named, the quota is shown as a measured fact, and the card clears itself when a write lands again. Dismissing it defers the card instead of deleting it.

## Description
A new pure module, `components/ui/storageRemedy.ts`, holds `remedyFor(trouble, {uid, estimate})`, which maps each kind to at most one primary action: quota -> 'save archive' (buildArchive/saveArchive, already written for the sign-out dialog), blocked/missing-store -> 'reload', non-storage with a studio phase -> 'open' (studioHref), unavailable -> none. It also holds `troubleReducer`: report / dismiss / ok events over an `active | deferred | clear` state that accumulates `phases`. stepStore gains `noteStorageOk(op)`, called on withStore's success path, which clears a storage trouble of the same op and never a `non-storage` one. NotificationBell feeds the reducer from `useStorageTrouble`, renders the phases as the existing mono `where` line (`script · frames · bookmark`), renders the quota fact as a `<Tally>` (`490/500 MB`, from `navigator.storage.estimate()`), and draws the verb beside 'dismiss' on the same compact text-button style as 'open'. A deferred trouble leaves the badge count but keeps the rose card as one row in the tray. Per CLAUDE.md, TROUBLE_WORD stays verbatim, because a real error explains itself. The card adds verbs and a number, not prose. Both worlds draw through the existing `k-tcard`/`k-tray__btn` classes and their Obsidian twins.

## Flow
- a quota write fails on Script -> the bell turns rose and the card shows `storage write failed`, the TROUBLE_WORD line, `script`, `490/500 MB` and [save archive] [dismiss]
- a second write fails on Frames -> the same card now reads `script · frames`; the badge stays 1
- the user presses save archive -> a .gravitone file downloads; the card stays because saving has not resumed
- the user deletes assets and edits again -> saveStep succeeds -> noteStorageOk('write') -> the card clears and a polite 'Saving again' announcement plays once
- dismiss instead -> the badge goes quiet and the row stays in the tray until a write lands

## Expected impact
The one moment the app knows work is at risk becomes a door to the fix rather than homework. The archive is one press away in every mode, not behind a sign-out. The user learns every step at risk, not just the last. The card stops saying 'nothing will be saved' after saving resumes, and stops forgetting that saving stopped when someone clicks dismiss.

## Evaluation
Claim: storage trouble is actionable per kind, names every step at risk, and is resolved by evidence (a successful write) instead of by a click.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (case 8 is a guard and passes; cases 1-7 fail, with no remedy module and no noteStorageOk)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - new tests/golden-path/storage-remedy.probe.spec.ts over storageRemedy.ts and stepStore's exported channel, Node probe lane, no DOM; announcement.probe and bell-doors.probe unchanged and green
Result: better
Gate: none
